dublinCore.title: Interactive STFT Spectrogram Analyzer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
Short-Time Fourier Transform
Spectrogram
Time-Frequency Resolution
Window Functions
dublinCore.description: A test signal built from two tones, two clicks, a chirp and noise is analyzed with the short-time Fourier transform twice, with a short and a long window. The two spectrograms share a time axis, each with the spectrum of the frame at the cursor, and cursors measure time and frequency separations.

topic: Window length, window type and hop size
learningObjectives: Compare spectrograms of one signal made with a short and a long window
Predict from the window length whether two tones or two clicks will be separated
Measure time and frequency separations on a spectrogram with cursors
Justify a choice of window length, window type and hop size for a given signal
Explain why the time span and the bin spacing of a window cannot both be made small
prerequisites: The DFT, bin spacing and window functions

misconceptions.misconception: There is one best window length for every signal
misconceptions.correction: A short window resolves events in time and a long window resolves components in frequency; which is better depends on what has to be separated
misconceptions.evidence: With the default spacings window A (N = 64) separates the clicks but merges the tones, and window B (N = 1024) does the opposite

misconceptions.misconception: A smaller hop size improves time resolution
misconceptions.correction: The hop size only sets how finely the spectrogram is sampled in time; the resolution is set by the window length and window type
misconceptions.evidence: Change the hop from N/2 to N/8: the picture has more columns but the click lines and tone lines keep the same width

misconceptions.misconception: Information that a spectrogram does not show has been destroyed
misconceptions.correction: Two clicks inside one long window are not separate in the picture, but their spacing is still encoded as ripples in the frame spectrum, 1/spacing hertz apart
misconceptions.evidence: Untick Two tones, set the click spacing to 4 ms and window B to 1024: the frame spectrum shows ripples 250 Hz apart

optimizations: Spectrograms are recomputed only when the signal, window length, hop size or window type changes
Each spectrogram is cached as one image pixel per frame and per bin

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Waveform and two spectrograms of the same test signal, one computed with a short window and one with a long window, each with the spectrum of the frame at the time cursor beside it. Checkboxes switch the tones, clicks, chirp and noise on and off; sliders set the tone spacing, the click spacing and the two window lengths; menus choose the window type and hop size. Clicking a spectrogram places the time and frequency cursor.

responsiveBreakpoints.description: Below 600 px the labels and captions are shortened, the frame spectra are narrower and the time axis shows fewer ticks

controls.label: Two tones
controls.description: Adds two steady sinusoids of amplitude 1 at 500 Hz and at 500 Hz plus the tone spacing

controls.label: Two clicks
controls.description: Adds two single-sample impulses of amplitude 8 at 500 ms and at 500 ms plus the click spacing

controls.label: Chirp
controls.description: Adds a sinusoid whose frequency rises from 1100 Hz at 0 s to 1900 Hz at 1 s (1300 Hz to 1700 Hz across the displayed 250 to 750 ms)

controls.label: Noise
controls.description: Adds white Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.2

controls.label: Tone spacing
controls.description: Sets the frequency difference between the two tones

controls.label: Click spacing
controls.description: Sets the time between the two clicks

controls.label: Window A: N
controls.description: Chooses the window length of spectrogram A from 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 and 2048 samples (slider position 0 to 6)

controls.label: Window B: N
controls.description: Chooses the window length of spectrogram B from 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 and 2048 samples (slider position 0 to 6)

controls.label: Window type
controls.description: Chooses the window function applied to every frame of both spectrograms

controls.label: Hop size H
controls.description: Chooses the step between successive frames as a fraction of the window length

visualElements.description: Waveform of the test signal with a bar for the samples each window uses at the cursor
Two spectrograms on a common time axis, 250 to 750 ms and 0 to 2000 Hz, drawn with the viridis colour map from -60 dB to 0 dB, with time and frequency cursors
Spectrum of the frame at the time cursor beside each spectrogram, on the same frequency axis
Caption of each spectrogram with N, window time span, bin spacing, and the tone and click spacings in the window's own units; cursor and pointer read-out

model.description: A synthetic 1 s signal sampled at 8000 Hz is cut into windowed frames and each frame is transformed with a radix-2 FFT of the same length as the window (no zero-padding). Magnitudes are scaled so that a bin-centred sinusoid of amplitude 1 reads 0 dB.
equations: X[m, k] = sum over n of x[n + m H] w[n] e^(-j 2 pi k n / N)
window time span = N / fs; bin spacing = fs / N; their product is 1
two impulses tau seconds apart have a spectrum with ripples every 1 / tau hertz
algorithms: Short-time Fourier transform with Hann, Hamming, Blackman and rectangular windows
assumptions: fs = 8000 Hz; the signal is 1 s long and 250 to 750 ms and 0 to 2000 Hz are displayed
Tones have amplitude 1, clicks are single samples of amplitude 8, the chirp rises from 1100 to 1900 Hz over the full second, and the noise has standard deviation 0.2
The FFT length equals the window length (no zero-padding)
The colour scale spans 60 dB; levels above 0 dB are drawn in the brightest colour

instructionalStrategies: Predict-then-verify using the bins-apart and windows-apart read-outs
Side-by-side comparison of two analyses of the same signal
Measure separations with the cursor and pointer
extensions: Add a speech or music recording and compare wideband and narrowband spectrograms
Add zero-padding to separate the effect of the FFT length from the window length
